scenes.audio: Marcus can no longer afford the continuing premiums on his whole life policy. Before he gives it up, he reviews its non-forfeiture choices.
scenes.label: Opening Hook
scenes.visual: Static camera angle. Marcus, a Black man in his early 40s with short hair and a dark blue shirt, sits at a wooden kitchen table next to Elena, a biracial woman in her late 30s with long dark hair and a sage green blouse. They are looking down at a white document. Marcus holds a silver pen. To their left is an open laptop. The kitchen background is softly lit with warm tones and natural light from a window.

scenes.audio: These choices use the value already built under the policy when premium payments stop. The familiar alternatives are taking available cash, using value for extended term insurance, or keeping a smaller amount of paid-up permanent insurance. They preserve different things. A no cash value term policy does not suddenly acquire those values because its premium is missed. Start with the actual policy, current values, and any outstanding debt, then compare what protection would remain under each available choice.
scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.visual: A clean graphic interface on a white background. Three rectangular boxes appear horizontally. The first is teal with the words 'Cash surrender'. The second is light blue with 'Extended term'. The third is light red with 'Reduced paid-up'. Text descriptions fade in below each title as the narrator speaks.

scenes.audio: Cash surrender pays the available surrender amount to the owner and ends the surrendered policy's protection. It is not an advanced death claim. Suppose the insurer's statement shows $12,000 available before a separately listed $2,000 policy debt with no other adjustment. The net cash payment is $10,000. If the quoted amount already includes that debt, do not deduct it again. Surrender can also have tax consequences, addressed in the tax lessons. The owner should understand the lost death protection before signing. A later change of mind does not create an automatic right to reinstate a cash surrendered policy.
scenes.label: Product Selling Points
scenes.visual: Graphic interface. A white box on the left shows '$12,000'. A middle box shows '- $2,000'. A final box on the right shows '$10,000'. Teal lines connect the boxes. The background is a mix of white and a light grey sidebar.

scenes.audio: Under the simplified extended term choice, the available value buys term protection at the original face amount for as long as that value purchases. No further premiums are required for that purchased period. Assume a debt-free policy with a $100,000 face amount. Its actual table offers $100,000 of extended term for 8 years. A covered death in year 7 falls within that period. Death in year 9 does not. 8 years comes from this hypothetical table, not a universal formula. Debt additions and the contract can affect the actual benefit and duration.
scenes.label: Product Selling Points
scenes.visual: Graphic flow chart. Three numbered boxes (01, 02, 03) appear from left to right. Box 01 says 'Available value'. Box 02 says '$100,000 for 8 years'. Box 03 says 'After year 8'. Teal arrows show the progression between the states.

scenes.audio: Reduced paid-up insurance uses available value to continue a smaller amount of permanent life protection with no further required premiums for that reduced base benefit. Assume the same policy offers $32,000 of reduced paid-up whole life. The family gives up part of the former $100,000 amount but keeps the smaller permanent benefit. This is different from paying the final scheduled premium on a limited pay contract and keeping its original promised amount. It is also different from purchasing paid-up additions with a dividend. Review whether riders continue and how debt affects the actual option.
scenes.label: Product Selling Points
scenes.visual: Graphic comparison table. The left column shows the 'Before' state with an original $100,000 policy. The middle column shows 'Reduced paid-up' with $32,000. The right column shows 'Future premiums' are none. The layout is clean with soft teal accents.

scenes.audio: Read the election deadline and automatic default. Maryland's standard provision for these choices gives the specified election opportunity within 60 days after the due date of the premium in default. If the entitled person does not choose another available option in that period, the policy's specified paid-up benefit takes effect. Do not automatically name extended term as the required default for every Maryland policy. Read the policy's own provision and the statute's applicability rules. The standard statute also distinguishes paid-up benefit eligibility from ordinary and industrial cash surrender minimums. A more favorable contract may provide value earlier. Contact the insurer promptly while the choice remains available.
scenes.label: Product Information
scenes.visual: Graphic sequence showing the timeline of an election. Box 01: 'Premium default'. Box 02: '60-day election'. Box 03: 'No election'. Arrows indicate the progression. The aesthetic remains consistent with the previous informational graphics.

scenes.audio: Marcus compares the three hypothetical offers. If his stated priority is $10,000 of immediate net cash and ending this protection...
scenes.label: Usage Scenarios
scenes.visual: Return to the initial scene. Marcus and Elena are still at the kitchen table. Marcus is pointing at the document with his pen while Elena leans in to look closely. The lighting remains warm and natural. The camera is static.

scenes.audio: ...cash surrender matches that objective. If he wants the stated $100,000 benefit for the next 8 years without more premiums, extended term matches it. If he wants some permanent protection without continuing premiums, the $32,000 reduced paid-up option matches that goal. Those are exam comparisons using supplied facts, not a recommendation for every family. Review current protection needs, remaining resources, tax effects, and the actual written values before an owner makes a real decision.
scenes.label: Call to Action
scenes.visual: Summary graphic. Four numbered points appear: 01 Cash now ($10,000), 02 Temporary larger benefit ($100,000 for 8 years), 03 Smaller permanent benefit ($32,000), 04 Real decision. The background is white with a light teal border at the top.
